_source: myDomains -> MyDomainsResponse { success, message, error, metadata, data: [DomainEntity!] }. DomainEntity introspected live: autoRenew!, createdAt!, expiresAt, id!, name!, nameservers:[String!]!, registeredAt!, status:DomainStatus!, updatedAt!, user. No relations are loaded, so `user` is null on the wire. Rows are ordered expiresAt ASC by the handler, so soonest-expiry first is the transport's own order and not a sort the screen applied. ONE CORRECTION TO A STALE NOTE CARRIED FROM THE SEALED CONSOLE CASE: DomainStatus.expiring IS written - domain-expiry.service.ts runs hourly and sets expiring/expired - so the row reads `status` directly and needs no browser-computed condition. THE REGISTRAR IS SIMULATED, which is why every row here shows ns1/ns2.nivo.vn and a 365-day term: addDomain writes exactly that, with no price and no WHOIS, and a fixture carrying a registrar price would be inventing a field.
